```python
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Sequence

from .log_parse import PytestReport
from .match import resolve_all
from .types import Grade, Instance

RESOLVED = "resolved"
UNRESOLVED = "unresolved"
UNSCORABLE = "unscorable"

#: Status words pytest prints for a test that passed. A strict xpass is reported as FAILED
#: by pytest itself, so it lands in `unresolved` through the normal path.
PASSING = ("PASSED", "XPASS")


def grade_run(
    instance: Instance,
    report: PytestReport,
    record_id: str,
    notes: Sequence[str] = (),
    patch_applied: bool = True,
    timed_out: bool = False,
) -> Grade:
    """Decide a record's label and reward from what the run actually showed.

    resolved    every required node id was reported and passed.
    unresolved  every required node id was reported and at least one did not pass.
    unscorable  the run cannot decide: no statuses, an internally inconsistent log, a
                timeout, or a required node id it never reported on. No reward is claimed.
    """
    resolved = resolve_all(report.statuses, instance.required_tests)
    missing = [node for node, status in resolved.items() if status is None]
    failed = [node for node, status in resolved.items() if status is not None and status not in PASSING]

    why: list[str] = list(notes)
    if timed_out:
        why.append("run timed out; its result is not usable")
    if not report.statuses:
        why.append("run reported no test statuses")
    why.extend(report.inconsistent)
    if missing:
        shown = ", ".join(missing[:3]) + (" ..." if len(missing) > 3 else "")
        why.append(f"{len(missing)} required node id(s) never reported: {shown}")

    if timed_out or not report.statuses or report.inconsistent or missing:
        label, reward = UNSCORABLE, None
    elif failed:
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
    else:
        label, reward = RESOLVED, 1.0

    if label == RESOLVED and not patch_applied:
        # The rollout's patch never made it into the checkout, so whatever the run showed,
        # it did not show the patch resolving the instance.
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
        why.append("submission patch did not apply; the run cannot credit it")

    return Grade(
        record_id=record_id,
        instance_id=instance.instance_id,
        reward=reward,
        label=label,
        statuses=dict(report.statuses),
        missing=missing,
        failed=failed,
        notes=why,
    )
```

```python
def run_command(argv, cwd, timeout_s=DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S) -> RunOutput:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
    env.pop("PYTEST_ADDOPTS", None)
    env.pop("PYTEST_PLUGINS", None)
    env["PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE"] = "1"
    env["PYTHONHASHSEED"] = "0"
    started = time.time()
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            list(argv), cwd=str(cwd), env=env,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, timeout=timeout_s,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        # Partial output is still worth keeping: it says what the run was doing.
        log = _decode(getattr(exc, "stdout", None))
        err = _decode(getattr(exc, "stderr", None))
        return RunOutput(command=" ".join(argv), exit_code=-1, log=log, seconds=time.time()-started, timed_out=True, stderr=err)
    return RunOutput(command=" ".join(argv), exit_code=completed.returncode,
                     log=_decode(completed.stdout), seconds=time.time()-started, stderr=_decode(completed.stderr))
```

arguments.content:
"""Turn a pytest log into per-test statuses.

The grading command forces `--verbose`, so pytest prints one progress line per test as the
run goes:

    tests/test_core.py::test_alpha PASSED                                    [ 33%]
    tests/test_core.py::test_beta SKIPPED (no driver)                        [ 66%]
    tests/test_x.py::test_param[a - b] FAILED                                [ 80%]

That is the only place a *green* run names its tests. The `short test summary info` section
the old parser read is printed only when something fails, and without `-rA` it then lists
only the failures -- so a run in which every required test passed produced no summary at
all, and the parse came back empty. That is what flattened the training pass to zero
reward: every record looked like "no information about anything", which the reward stage
then paid out as zero.

The parser therefore reads the progress lines. Node ids are kept whole (`file.py::Class::
test[param]`, including the spaces a parametrised id can contain), and the status is the
exact word pytest printed. The final banner (`=== 2 passed, 1 failed in 0.21s ===`) is
parsed as well: a log whose progress lines and banner account for different numbers of
outcomes is not a transcript any honest pytest run produces, and the run is marked
inconsistent so the reward stage can treat it as unscorable instead of trusting it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

# One verbose progress line: the node id, the status word, an optional parenthesised reason
# (pytest truncates it itself, e.g. `XFAIL (h...)`), and the progress percentage. The node
# id is matched greedily so the *last* status word before the percentage wins -- a
# parametrised id may itself contain a word like PASSED.
PROGRESS_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<node>.*\S)"
    r"\s+(?P<status>PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|SKIPPED|XFAIL(?:ED)?|XPASS(?:ED)?)"
    r"(?:\s+\((?:[^()]*(?:\([^()]*\))?[^()]*)\))?"
    r"\s+\[\s*\d+%\]\s*$"
)

# The final banner line: `========================= 2 passed, 1 failed in 0.21s =========================`.
RESULT_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^=+\s*(?P<body>.+?)\s*=+$")

# The outcome counts inside the banner.
COUNT_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?P<n>\d+)\s+(?P<kind>passed|failed|errors?|skipped|xfailed|xpassed|deselected|warnings?)"
)

# Outcomes the banner counts but that never print a progress line.
UNCOUNTED_KINDS = ("deselected", "warning", "warnings")

NO_TESTS_RAN = "no tests ran"


@dataclass
class PytestReport:
    """What one pytest run's own log says about the tests it ran."""

    # node id -> status word, exactly as printed. A test that passes its call phase and
    # then errors in teardown is reported twice; the later line wins.
    statuses: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # How many progress lines were seen (a node id can appear on more than one).
    reported: int = 0
    # The final banner line, when the run got far enough to print one.
    result_line: str | None = None
    # How many outcomes the banner accounts for.
    counted: int | None = None
    # Reasons the log cannot be trusted as a transcript of the run.
    inconsistent: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def parse_progress(log: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], int]:
    """Read the per-test statuses out of the verbose progress lines."""
    statuses: dict[str, str] = {}
    lines = 0
    for line in log.splitlines():
        match = PROGRESS_RE.match(line)
        if match is None:
            continue
        lines += 1
        statuses[match.group("node")] = match.group("status")
    return statuses, lines


def parse_result_line(log: str) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
    """The run's final banner and the number of test outcomes it accounts for."""
    for line in reversed(log.splitlines()):
        match = RESULT_LINE_RE.match(line)
        if match is None:
            continue
        body = match.group("body")
        if NO_TESTS_RAN in body:
            return line, 0
        counts = COUNT_RE.findall(body)
        if not counts:
            continue  # a section header (``=== short test summary info ===``), not a result
        return line, sum(
            int(n) for n, kind in counts if kind not in UNCOUNTED_KINDS
        )
    return None, None


def parse_pytest_log(log: str | None) -> PytestReport:
    """Parse one pytest run's log: statuses plus the banner cross-check."""
    report = PytestReport()
    if not log:
        return report
    report.statuses, report.reported = parse_progress(log)
    report.result_line, report.counted = parse_result_line(log)
    if not report.statuses:
        # Nothing ran or nothing was reported: a usage error, an interrupted collection,
        # a crash. There is nothing to cross-check; the reward stage scores it unscorable.
        return report
    if report.counted is None:
        report.inconsistent.append(
            f"no result banner after {report.reported} progress line(s)"
        )
    elif report.counted != report.reported:
        report.inconsistent.append(
            f"result banner accounts for {report.counted} outcome(s) "
            f"but {report.reported} progress line(s) were reported"
        )
    return report

arguments.content:
"""Match the node ids a corpus instance requires against the statuses a run reported.

Node ids are matched exactly. The previous matcher tried to bridge "spelling drift" by
dropping the file part of every id and then falling back to the first entry that merely
*contained* the required name -- so a required `...::test_email_validation` could be
answered by any longer id that had it as a substring, for instance a passing
`...::test_email_validation_with_none`, and a passing test started deciding the fate of a
different, failing one. Worse, the same fallback silently satisfied ids the suite does not
have.

The corpus ids are full pytest node ids and pytest reports that same spelling, so exact
equality is the whole rule. A required id the run never reports is exactly the case the
reward contract calls *unscorable*: the run never reported on it, and no neighbour's status
may stand in for it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Iterable, Mapping


def lookup(
    statuses: Mapping[str, str], node_id: str
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    """Resolve one required node id against the parsed statuses.

    Returns (key, status): the entry the node id resolved to, or (None, None) when the run
    said nothing about exactly this id.
    """
    if node_id in statuses:
        return node_id, statuses[node_id]

arguments.content:
"""Turn a parsed pytest run into the label and reward the trainer consumes.

The corpus protocol is all-or-nothing over the instance's required node ids: a rollout is
rewarded when every required test passes -- the tests the bug broke and the tests that were
already green -- and a patch that trades one broken test for another earns nothing. The
three outcomes of the reward contract are kept strictly apart:

* ``resolved``   -- the run reported every required node id, and every one of them passed.
* ``unresolved`` -- the run reported every required node id, and at least one did not pass.
* ``unscorable`` -- the run could not decide: it reported no statuses at all, its log is not
  internally consistent, it timed out, or it never reported on some required node id. These
  records carry ``reward=None``; a zero is a claim about the patch, not a way to say "no
  information", so the trainer drops them instead of learning from a number that claims
  nothing.

The old stage collapsed all of the last group into ``reward=0.0``: an empty parse (a green
run the old parser could not read) was paid out exactly like a genuine failure, which is
what zeroed the whole training pass.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Sequence

from .log_parse import PytestReport
from .match import resolve_all
from .types import Grade, Instance

RESOLVED = "resolved"
UNRESOLVED = "unresolved"
UNSCORABLE = "unscorable"

# The status words pytest prints for a test that passed. A strict xpass is printed as
# FAILED by pytest itself, so it reaches `unresolved` through the normal path.
PASSING = ("PASSED", "XPASS")


def grade_run(
    instance: Instance,
    report: PytestReport,
    record_id: str,
    notes: Sequence[str] = (),
    patch_applied: bool = True,
    timed_out: bool = False,
) -> Grade:
    """Decide one record's label and reward from what the run actually showed."""
    resolved = resolve_all(report.statuses, instance.required_tests)
    missing = [node for node, status in resolved.items() if status is None]
    failed = [
        node
        for node, status in resolved.items()
        if status is not None and status not in PASSING
    ]

    why: list[str] = list(notes)
    if timed_out:
        why.append("run timed out; its log is not a finished result")
    if not report.statuses:
        why.append("run reported no test statuses")
    why.extend(report.inconsistent)
    if missing:
        shown = ", ".join(missing[:3]) + (" ..." if len(missing) > 3 else "")
        why.append(f"{len(missing)} required node id(s) never reported: {shown}")

    if timed_out or not report.statuses or report.inconsistent or missing:
        label, reward = UNSCORABLE, None
    elif failed:
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
    else:
        label, reward = RESOLVED, 1.0

    if label == RESOLVED and not patch_applied:
        # Whatever the run showed, it did not show it with this rollout's patch in the
        # checkout -- the patch never made it in, so it cannot be credited.
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
        why.append("submission patch did not apply; the run cannot credit it")

    return Grade(
        record_id=record_id,
        instance_id=instance.instance_id,
        reward=reward,
        label=label,
        statuses=dict(report.statuses),
        missing=missing,
        failed=failed,
        notes=why,
    )

"""Turn a parsed pytest run into the label and reward the trainer consumes.

The corpus protocol is all-or-nothing over the instance's required node ids: a rollout is
rewarded when every required test passes -- the tests the bug broke and the tests that were
already green -- and a patch that trades one broken test for another earns nothing. The
three outcomes of the reward contract are kept strictly apart:

* ``resolved``   -- the run reported every required node id, and every one of them passed.
* ``unresolved`` -- the run reported every required node id, and at least one did not pass.
* ``unscorable`` -- the run could not decide: it reported no statuses at all, its log is not
  internally consistent, it timed out, or it never reported on some required node id. These
  records carry ``reward=None``; a zero is a claim about the patch, not a way to say "no
  information", so the trainer drops them instead of learning from a number that claims
  nothing.

The old stage collapsed all of the last group into ``reward=0.0``: an empty parse (a green
run the old parser could not read) was paid out exactly like a genuine failure, which is
what zeroed the whole training pass.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Sequence

from .log_parse import PytestReport
from .match import resolve_all
from .types import Grade, Instance

RESOLVED = "resolved"
UNRESOLVED = "unresolved"
UNSCORABLE = "unscorable"

# The status words pytest prints for a test that passed. A strict xpass is printed as
# FAILED by pytest itself, so it reaches `unresolved` through the normal path.
PASSING = ("PASSED", "XPASS")


def grade_run(
    instance: Instance,
    report: PytestReport,
    record_id: str,
    notes: Sequence[str] = (),
    patch_applied: bool = True,
    timed_out: bool = False,
) -> Grade:
    """Decide one record's label and reward from what the run actually showed."""
    resolved = resolve_all(report.statuses, instance.required_tests)
    missing = [node for node, status in resolved.items() if status is None]
    failed = [
        node
        for node, status in resolved.items()
        if status is not None and status not in PASSING
    ]

    why: list[str] = list(notes)
    if timed_out:
        why.append("run timed out; its log is not a finished result")
    if not report.statuses:
        why.append("run reported no test statuses")
    why.extend(report.inconsistent)
    if missing:
        shown = ", ".join(missing[:3]) + (" ..." if len(missing) > 3 else "")
        why.append(f"{len(missing)} required node id(s) never reported: {shown}")

    if timed_out or not report.statuses or report.inconsistent or missing:
        label, reward = UNSCORABLE, None
    elif failed:
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
    else:
        label, reward = RESOLVED, 1.0

    if label == RESOLVED and not patch_applied:
        # Whatever the run showed, it did not show it with this rollout's patch in the
        # checkout -- the patch never made it in, so it cannot be credited.
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
        why.append("submission patch did not apply; the run cannot credit it")

    return Grade(
        record_id=record_id,
        instance_id=instance.instance_id,
        reward=reward,
        label=label,
        statuses=dict(report.statuses),
        missing=missing,
        failed=failed,
        notes=why,
    )

arguments.content:
"""Freeze the instance's exam and restore it after the rollout's patch is applied.

A rollout patch may touch anything in the checkout, and the corpus contains submissions
that do exactly what a reward pipeline must not tolerate: stub required tests out with
`def test_x(*args, **kwargs): pass`, add a root `conftest.py` whose `pytest_runtest_makereport`
hook rewrites every failure into a pass, add a `pytest.ini` whose addopts load such a
plugin, or append their own passing test inside a required test file. The reward has to
describe what the repository's tests actually do with the patch, not what the rollout
changed them to say.

So the exam is snapshotted byte-for-byte right after the instance bug is injected -- while
the checkout still holds exactly what the instance defines -- and restored just before the
tests run, after the rollout's patch. The exam is every file that decides what is tested
and how the run reports it:

* the files that hold the instance's required node ids;
* every `conftest.py` and every pytest configuration file (`pytest.ini`, `tox.ini`,
  `setup.cfg`, `pyproject.toml`) anywhere in the checkout;
* every test file (`test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `tests.py`, `test_*.md`, `tests.md`) anywhere,
  whatever directory the repository keeps them in;
* every file under a directory that holds such test files -- the helpers and data the
  tests import (`tests/base.py`, `tests/consts.py`, ...). The repository root itself is
  never swept this way: some projects keep a test file next to the package (a root-level
  `test_addict.py`), and the package source is precisely what the rollout is supposed to
  change.

Restoring rewrites those files to the snapshotted bytes and deletes the ones the checkout
did not have: a rollout cannot weaken a test, silence a hook, grow a new test file, or
keep a tampered one. Files outside the exam -- the package source the rollout is supposed
to fix -- pass through untouched.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable, Mapping

CONFIG_BASENAMES = ("conftest.py", "pytest.ini", "tox.ini", "setup.cfg", "pyproject.toml")

# The file spellings pytest collects by default and the ones the corpus repositories
# configure (`python_files = tests.py`, doctest globs over `*.md`).
TEST_FILE_PATTERNS = ("test_*.py", "*_test.py", "tests.py", "test_*.md", "tests.md")

# Nothing inside these belongs to the exam, and walking them would only waste time.
SKIP_DIRS = frozenset(
    {".git", "__pycache__", ".pytest_cache", ".tox", "node_modules", "venv", ".venv"}
)


def _is_test_file(name: str) -> bool:
    return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pattern) for pattern in TEST_FILE_PATTERNS)


def _walk(repo_root: Path):
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(repo_root):
        dirnames[:] = sorted(d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS)
        yield Path(dirpath), sorted(filenames)


def exam_files(repo_root: Path, required_files: Iterable[str] = ()) -> set[str]:
    """Every file of the checkout that belongs to the exam, as ``/``-separated paths.

    `required_files` are the file parts of the instance's required node ids; a repository
    that collects them under a non-default name still has them snapshotted.
    """
    required = set(required_files)
    exam: set[str] = set()
    test_dirs: set[str] = set()
    for directory, filenames in _walk(repo_root):
        for name in filenames:
            rel = (directory / name).relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
            if name in CONFIG_BASENAMES:
                exam.add(rel)
            if _is_test_file(name) or rel in required:
                exam.add(rel)
                # A directory that holds test files is a test directory -- but never the
                # repository root itself (see the module docstring).
                if "/" in rel:
                    test_dirs.add(rel.rsplit("/", 1)[0])
    for directory, filenames in _walk(repo_root):
        for name in filenames:
            rel = (directory / name).relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
            if any(rel == d or rel.startswith(d + "/") for d in test_dirs):
                exam.add(rel)
    return exam


def snapshot_exam(repo_root: Path, required_files: Iterable[str] = ()) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    """Byte-for-byte copy of the exam, keyed by relative path."""
    snapshot: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    for rel in sorted(exam_files(repo_root, required_files)):
        path = repo_root / rel
        if path.is_file():
            snapshot[rel] = path.read_bytes()
    return snapshot


def restore_exam(repo_root: Path, snapshot: Mapping[str, bytes]) -> list[str]:
    """Put the exam back to its snapshotted bytes.

    Files the checkout grew after the snapshot -- a rollout's `conftest.py`, a `pytest.ini`,
    a stubbed or newly added test file -- are removed; files it lost are written back.
    Returns notes for the record describing what was undone.
    """
    removed: list[str] = []
    for rel in sorted(exam_files(repo_root)):
        if rel not in snapshot:
            (repo_root / rel).unlink()
            removed.append(rel)
    rewritten: list[str] = []
    for rel, data in sorted(snapshot.items()):
        path = repo_root / rel
        if not path.is_file() or path.read_bytes() != data:
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_bytes(data)
            rewritten.append(rel)

    notes: list[str] = []
    if rewritten:
        notes.append(f"exam-restored: rewrote {', '.join(rewritten[:4])}"
                     + (" ..." if len(rewritten) > 4 else ""))
    if removed:
        notes.append(f"exam-restored: removed {', '.join(removed[:4])}"
                     + (" ..." if len(removed) > 4 else ""))
    return notes

"""Restore the instance's tests before a record is graded.

The policy works in the same checkout the grader then tests. Nothing stops a rollout from
editing the tests it is supposed to make pass, so the grading step puts the test files back to
their pristine state first: the reward has to describe the repository's behaviour, not the
rollout's opinion of it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

TEST_FILE_PATTERNS = ("test_*.py", "*_test.py")


def iter_test_files(repo_root: Path):
    """Every test file of the checkout, as paths relative to the repository root."""
    for pattern in TEST_FILE_PATTERNS:
        for path in sorted(repo_root.rglob(pattern)):
            if ".git" in path.parts:
                continue
            yield path.relative_to(repo_root)


def restore_tests(repo_root: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Check the test files out of git again. Returns the files that were restored."""
    restored = []
    for rel in iter_test_files(repo_root):
        subprocess.run(
            f"git checkout -- {rel} 2>/dev/null",
            shell=True,
            cwd=str(repo_root),
        )
        restored.append(str(rel))
    return restored

"""Run one grading command and hand back its log.

Grading runs are untrusted: the command executes code the policy just wrote, in the policy's
own checkout. It gets a wall-clock budget and its output is captured whole; nothing here
inspects the log.

Stdout is the transcript the parser reads. Stderr is captured too, separately: pytest
prints its usage errors there and prints nothing on stdout, and a run that failed to start
must stay diagnosable from the record's artifact instead of looking like an empty green
log. On a timeout the partial output is kept for the same reason.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from .types import RunOutput

DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 900


def _decode(raw: bytes | None) -> str:
    return raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if raw else ""


def run_command(argv: Sequence[str], cwd: Path, timeout_s: int = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S) -> RunOutput:
    env = dict(os.environ)
    # Keep the policy's environment out of the grading run, and keep the run deterministic.
    env.pop("PYTHONPATH", None)
    # Nothing outside the command line may add pytest arguments or autoload plugins.
    env.pop("PYTEST_ADDOPTS", None)
    env.pop("PYTEST_PLUGINS", None)
    env["PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE"] = "1"
    env["PYTHONHASHSEED"] = "0"
    started = time.time()
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            list(argv),
            cwd=str(cwd),
            env=env,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
            timeout=timeout_s,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        # The partial transcript still says what the run was doing when it was cut off.
        return RunOutput(
            command=" ".join(argv),
            exit_code=-1,
            log=_decode(getattr(exc, "stdout", None)),
            seconds=time.time() - started,
            timed_out=True,
            stderr=_decode(getattr(exc, "stderr", None)),
        )
    return RunOutput(
        command=" ".join(argv),
        exit_code=completed.returncode,
        log=_decode(completed.stdout),
        seconds=time.time() - started,
        stderr=_decode(completed.stderr),
    )

1. Primary Request and Intent:

The user's single task message: **"Repair the reward pipeline"** — the workspace holds the reward side of an agentic RL run on repository-repair tasks: grading pipeline (`rlgrade/`), rollout corpus (`corpus/`), per-repo environments (`.venvs/`), harness entry point (`scripts/regrade_run.py`), unit tests (`tests/`), and logs of an earlier grading pass (`logs/historical/`). Requirements (verbatim key clauses):

- Decide whether the pipeline reports what it claims; if not, find root cause(s) and repair them in the staged workspace at `/workspace` so "the label and reward of every record describe what the repository's own tests actually do with that rollout's patch." "Do not assume a stage is at fault without connecting it to observed behaviour, and do not stop at the first contributing factor you find."
- **"Do not use the network."** Everything needed is staged locally.
- May run the pipeline: `python3 -B scripts/regrade_run.py --out /tmp/<yours>` (CPU-only, suites take seconds).
- **Contract** (system re-runs `python3 -B scripts/regrade_run.py` and reads `experiment_logs/regrade.jsonl`; one line per record): `label` ∈ {`resolved`, `unresolved`, `unscorable`}; `reward` = `1.0` when resolved, `0.0` when unresolved, `null` when unscorable.
  - `resolved` — "the run showed that every required node id of the instance (`fail_to_pass + pass_to_pass`) passed with this rollout's patch applied."

```python
PROGRESS_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<node>.*\S)"
    r"\s+(?P<status>PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|SKIPPED|XFAIL(?:ED)?|XPASS(?:ED)?)"
    r"(?:\s+\((?:[^()]*(?:\([^()]*\))?[^()]*)\))?"
    r"\s+\[\s*\d+%\]\s*$"
)
RESULT_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^=+\s*(?P<body>.+?)\s*=+$")
COUNT_RE = re.compile(r"(?P<n>\d+)\s+(?P<kind>passed|failed|errors?|skipped|xfailed|xpassed|deselected|warnings?)")
UNCOUNTED_KINDS = ("deselected", "warning", "warnings")
NO_TESTS_RAN = "no tests ran"

@dataclass
class PytestReport:
    statuses: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)  # node id -> status word
    reported: int = 0          # progress lines seen (a node can appear twice)
    result_line: str | None = None
    counted: int | None = None
    inconsistent: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

def parse_progress(log: str) -> tuple[dict[str, str], int]:
    statuses: dict[str, str] = {}
    lines = 0
    for line in log.splitlines():
        match = PROGRESS_RE.match(line)
        if match is None:
            continue
        lines += 1
        statuses[match.group("node")] = match.group("status")  # later line wins
    return statuses, lines

def parse_result_line(log: str) -> tuple[str | None, int | None]:
    # reversed search; "no tests ran" -> (line, 0); counts summed excluding UNCOUNTED_KINDS;
    # lines with no counts (section headers) are skipped; returns (None, None) if no banner

def parse_pytest_log(log: str | None) -> PytestReport:
    report = PytestReport()
    if not log:
        return report
    report.statuses, report.reported = parse_progress(log)
    report.result_line, report.counted = parse_result_line(log)
    if not report.statuses:
        return report
    if report.counted is None:
        report.inconsistent.append(f"no result banner after {report.reported} progress line(s)")
    elif report.counted != report.reported:
        report.inconsistent.append(f"result banner accounts for {report.counted} outcome(s) but {report.reported} progress line(s) were reported")
    return report
```
Greedy `.*\S` node means the LAST status word before `[ NN%]` wins (param ids containing status words parse correctly). `normalize_node_id` REMOVED. Count cross-check compares against progress-LINE count (not dict size — teardown-error case).

```python
def lookup(statuses: Mapping[str, str], node_id: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
```

```python
RESOLVED = "resolved"; UNRESOLVED = "unresolved"; UNSCORABLE = "unscorable"
PASSING = ("PASSED", "XPASS")

def grade_run(instance: Instance, report: PytestReport, record_id: str,
              notes: Sequence[str] = (), patch_applied: bool = True,
              timed_out: bool = False) -> Grade:
    resolved = resolve_all(report.statuses, instance.required_tests)
    missing = [node for node, status in resolved.items() if status is None]
    failed = [node for node, status in resolved.items()
              if status is not None and status not in PASSING]
    why: list[str] = list(notes)
    if timed_out: why.append("run timed out; its log is not a finished result")
    if not report.statuses: why.append("run reported no test statuses")
    why.extend(report.inconsistent)
    if missing:
        shown = ", ".join(missing[:3]) + (" ..." if len(missing) > 3 else "")
        why.append(f"{len(missing)} required node id(s) never reported: {shown}")
    if timed_out or not report.statuses or report.inconsistent or missing:
        label, reward = UNSCORABLE, None
    elif failed:
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
    else:
        label, reward = RESOLVED, 1.0
    if label == RESOLVED and not patch_applied:
        label, reward = UNRESOLVED, 0.0
        why.append("submission patch did not apply; the run cannot credit it")
    return Grade(record_id=record_id, instance_id=instance.instance_id, reward=reward,
                 label=label, statuses=dict(report.statuses), missing=missing,
                 failed=failed, notes=why)
```

```python
CONFIG_BASENAMES = ("conftest.py", "pytest.ini", "tox.ini", "setup.cfg", "pyproject.toml")
TEST_FILE_PATTERNS = ("test_*.py", "*_test.py", "tests.py", "test_*.md", "tests.md")
SKIP_DIRS = frozenset({".git", "__pycache__", ".pytest_cache", ".tox", "node_modules", "venv", ".venv"})

def _is_test_file(name): return any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, p) for p in TEST_FILE_PATTERNS)
def _walk(repo_root):
    for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(repo_root):
        dirnames[:] = sorted(d for d in dirnames if d not in SKIP_DIRS)
        yield Path(dirpath), sorted(filenames)

def exam_files(repo_root: Path, required_files: Iterable[str] = ()) -> set[str]:
    required = set(required_files)
    exam: set[str] = set(); test_dirs: set[str] = set()
    for directory, filenames in _walk(repo_root):
        for name in filenames:
            rel = (directory / name).relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
            if name in CONFIG_BASENAMES: exam.add(rel)
            if _is_test_file(name) or rel in required:
                exam.add(rel)
                if "/" in rel: test_dirs.add(rel.rsplit("/", 1)[0])  # never repo root
    for directory, filenames in _walk(repo_root):
        for name in filenames:
            rel = (directory / name).relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
            if any(rel == d or rel.startswith(d + "/") for d in test_dirs):
                exam.add(rel)
    return exam

def snapshot_exam(repo_root, required_files=()) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    snapshot = {}
    for rel in sorted(exam_files(repo_root, required_files)):
        path = repo_root / rel
        if path.is_file(): snapshot[rel] = path.read_bytes()
    return snapshot

def restore_exam(repo_root, snapshot: Mapping[str, bytes]) -> list[str]:
    removed = []
    for rel in sorted(exam_files(repo_root)):          # name rules only
        if rel not in snapshot:
            (repo_root / rel).unlink(); removed.append(rel)
    rewritten = []
    for rel, data in sorted(snapshot.items()):
        path = repo_root / rel
        if not path.is_file() or path.read_bytes() != data:
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_bytes(data); rewritten.append(rel)
    notes = []
    if rewritten: notes.append("exam-restored: rewrote " + ", ".join(rewritten[:4]) + (" ..." if len(rewritten) > 4 else ""))
    if removed: notes.append("exam-restored: removed " + ", ".join(removed[:4]) + (" ..." if len(removed) > 4 else ""))
    return notes
```

Final design decisions (all settled):
- **Exact node-id matching only**; required id never reported → `unscorable` (reward None) — the contract's clause "it never reported on a required node id" maps to the 8 truncated-id instances (50 records). Truncated ids are FULL node ids and snapshots have one commit, so unspoofable and unrecoverable; a rollout adding `def test_colored` to the required file gets reverted by exam restore.
- PASSING = ("PASSED", "XPASS"); SKIPPED/XFAIL/FAILED/ERROR on a required id → unresolved 0.0 (run reported it, it did not pass).
- **Patch-failed**: run proceeds on the unpatched tree (old behavior), label from the run; if the run would say resolved → forced UNRESOLVED 0.0 with note (a patch that doesn't apply can't be credited); if required ids missing → unscorable dominates. Empty-patch → proceeds (trivially applied) → typically unresolved 0.0.
- Timeout → unscorable. Materialize failure (bug patch) → unscorable (corpus broken, not rollout's fault). `grade_record` NEVER raises (outer try/except → unscorable Grade with `grader-error:` note).
- Snapshot order: materialize (bug applied) → **snapshot_exam(repo, test_files(instance))** → apply_submission → **restore_exam(repo, snapshot)** → run. (Snapshot MUST be before submission apply, else tampering gets frozen as pristine.)
- Count cross-check: banner counts (passed+failed+errors+skipped+xfailed+xpassed, excluding deselected/warnings) vs progress-LINE count; mismatch or missing banner (with statuses present) → inconsistent → unscorable. This also defends against phantom injected PASSED lines (pytest captures prints from test code; conftest prints are moot after restore).
- Executor: stderr captured separately (usage errors visible in artifact, never parsed); pop PYTEST_ADDOPTS and PYTEST_PLUGINS; keep partial output on TimeoutExpired (exc.stdout).
- `rollout_report_plugin.py` at root survives restore as inert orphan (pytest.ini reverted → never loaded) — acceptable, documented.

"""Construction of the pytest command used to grade one record.

from typing import Sequence

from .types import Instance

    files: dict[str, None] = {}

    """argv of the grading run for one instance."""
    argv = [str(instance.env_python), "-m", "pytest"]
    argv.extend(BASE_FLAGS)
    argv.extend(instance.extra_args)
    argv.extend(files if files is not None else test_files(instance))
    return argv

"""The grading pipeline: record in, reward out.

Each record is graded in a scratch checkout of its instance:

    pristine snapshot -> inject the instance bug -> apply the rollout patch ->
    restore the tests -> run the required test files -> parse -> reward

The scratch checkout is a git repository, so the bug and the patch can be applied and undone
with the same tools the rollout itself used, and `git status` tells the trainer what a rollout
touched.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from .command import build_command, test_files
from .executor import run_command
from .log_parse import parse_pytest_log
from .reset import restore_tests
from .reward import grade_statuses
from .types import Grade, Instance, Submission


def _git(repo_root: Path, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=str(repo_root),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )


def materialize(instance: Instance, scratch: Path) -> Path:
    """Copy the pristine snapshot into the scratch directory and inject the instance bug."""
    repo = scratch / instance.repo_key
    if repo.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(repo)
    shutil.copytree(instance.repo_root, repo, symlinks=True)
    _git(repo, "reset", "--hard", "HEAD")
    _git(repo, "clean", "-qfd")

"""The grading pipeline: record in, reward out.

Each record is graded in a scratch checkout of its instance:

    pristine snapshot -> inject the instance bug -> snapshot the exam ->
    apply the rollout patch -> restore the exam -> run the required test files ->
    parse -> reward

The order is the whole defense. The exam -- every file that decides what is tested and how
the run reports it, see `reset` -- is snapshotted while the checkout still holds exactly
what the instance defines, and restored *after* the rollout's patch: whatever the rollout
changed about the suite (a stubbed test, a hook that rewrites reports, a configuration that
loads one) is undone before a single test runs, while the source the rollout is supposed to
fix passes through.

Two promises hold for every record, whatever fails along the way:

* the rollout never gets to decide its own exam, and
* a record the run could not decide is reported `unscorable` with reward ``None`` -- never
  a zero, which would be a claim about the patch the run never made.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from .command import build_command, test_files
from .executor import run_command
from .log_parse import parse_pytest_log
from .reset import restore_exam, snapshot_exam
from .reward import UNSCORABLE, grade_run
from .types import Grade, Instance, RunOutput, Submission


def _git_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    """A git environment that reads no user or system config.

    The grading sandbox denies access to `/root/.gitconfig`, and a git that dies reading its
    config leaves the checkout exactly as it was while reporting nothing useful. Pointing
    the config at `/dev/null` makes git work the same inside and outside the sandbox.
    """
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM"] = "1"
    return env


def _git(repo_root: Path, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=str(repo_root),
        env=_git_env(),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )


def materialize(instance: Instance, scratch: Path) -> Path:
    """Copy the pristine snapshot into the scratch directory and inject the instance bug."""
    repo = scratch / instance.repo_key
    if repo.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(repo)
    shutil.copytree(instance.repo_root, repo, symlinks=True)
    _git(repo, "reset", "--hard", "HEAD")
    _git(repo, "clean", "-qfd")
    patch_path = scratch / "bug.patch"
    patch_path.write_text(instance.bug_patch, encoding="utf-8")
    applied = _git(repo, "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(patch_path))
    if applied.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{instance.instance_id}: bug patch did not apply: {applied.stdout[-400:]}"
        )
    return repo


def _patch_targets(patch_text: str) -> list[str]:
    """The paths a unified diff writes to (its `+++ b/...` lines)."""
    targets = []
    for line in patch_text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            targets.append(line[len("+++ b/"):].strip())
        elif line.startswith("+++ "):
            targets.append(line[len("+++ "):].strip())
    return targets


def _escapes_checkout(target: str) -> bool:
    """True when a patch target names something outside the checkout.

    An empty path, an absolute path, or one that climbs with `..` would write outside the
    scratch tree the grader controls.
    """
    if not target or target in ("/dev/null",):
        return False
    if target.startswith("/"):
        return True
    parts = Path(target).parts
    return any(part == ".." for part in parts)


def apply_submission(repo: Path, submission: Submission, scratch: Path) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Apply the rollout patch into the checkout.

    Returns (applied, notes). The run proceeds on the unpatched tree when the patch does not
    apply -- the instance's own tests still describe that tree -- but a run that passes there
    cannot be credited to the patch, so `grade_run` demotes it.
    """
    if not submission.patch.strip():
        return True, ["empty-patch: no patch in the submission; run proceeds on the unpatched tree"]
    for target in _patch_targets(submission.patch):
        if _escapes_checkout(target):
            return False, [f"patch-rejected: target leaves the checkout: {target}"]
    patch_path = scratch / "submission.patch"
    patch_path.write_text(submission.patch, encoding="utf-8")
    applied = _git(repo, "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(patch_path))
    if applied.returncode != 0:
        applied = subprocess.run(
            ["patch", "-p1", "--forward", "--batch", "-i", str(patch_path)],
            cwd=str(repo),
            env=_git_env(),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            text=True,
        )
    if applied.returncode == 0:
        return True, []
    tail = (applied.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["no output"]
    return False, ["patch-failed: " + tail[0][:200]]


def _write_log(scratch: Path, run: RunOutput) -> None:
    """The record's artifact: the parsed transcript, plus stderr when there was any."""
    text = run.log
    if run.stderr.strip():
        text += "\n\n----- stderr -----\n" + run.stderr
    if run.timed_out:
        text += "\n\n----- timed out -----\n"
    (scratch / "pytest.log").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def _grade_record(instance: Instance, submission: Submission, scratch: Path, timeout_s: int) -> Grade:
    repo = materialize(instance, scratch)
    exam = snapshot_exam(repo, test_files(instance))
    applied, notes = apply_submission(repo, submission, scratch)
    notes = notes + restore_exam(repo, exam)
    run = run_command(build_command(instance, test_files(instance)), cwd=repo, timeout_s=timeout_s)
    _write_log(scratch, run)
    notes = notes + [f"exit={run.exit_code}", f"seconds={run.seconds:.1f}"]
    report = parse_pytest_log(run.log)
    return grade_run(
        instance,
        report,
        submission.record_id,
        notes=notes,
        patch_applied=applied,
        timed_out=run.timed_out,
    )


def grade_record(
    instance: Instance,
    submission: Submission,
    scratch: Path,
    timeout_s: int = 900,
) -> Grade:
    """Grade one record; never raise.

    Whatever fails -- the corpus snapshot is unreadable, the bug patch does not apply, a
    grading tool dies -- the record still gets a `Grade`, and a run that never happened is
    `unscorable` with reward ``None``: the harness's own error fallback would pay it out as
    a 0.0, which is a claim about a patch nothing ever tested.
    """
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    try:
        return _grade_record(instance, submission, scratch, timeout_s)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - the record must be decided, not dropped
        why = [f"grader-error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"]
        return Grade(
            record_id=submission.record_id,
            instance_id=instance.instance_id,
            reward=None,
            label=UNSCORABLE,
            missing=list(instance.required_tests),
            notes=why,
        )

"""The grading pipeline: record in, reward out.

Each record is graded in a scratch checkout of its instance:

    pristine snapshot -> inject the instance bug -> snapshot the exam ->
    apply the rollout patch -> restore the exam -> run the required test files ->
    parse -> reward

The order is the whole defense. The exam -- every file that decides what is tested and how
the run reports it, see `reset` -- is snapshotted while the checkout still holds exactly
what the instance defines, and restored *after* the rollout's patch: whatever the rollout
changed about the suite (a stubbed test, a hook that rewrites reports, a configuration that
loads one) is undone before a single test runs, while the source the rollout is supposed to
fix passes through.

Two promises hold for every record, whatever fails along the way:

* the rollout never gets to decide its own exam, and
* a record the run could not decide is reported `unscorable` with reward ``None`` -- never
  a zero, which would be a claim about the patch the run never made.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Sequence

from .command import build_command, test_files
from .executor import run_command
from .log_parse import parse_pytest_log
from .reset import restore_exam, snapshot_exam
from .reward import UNSCORABLE, grade_run
from .types import Grade, Instance, RunOutput, Submission


def _git_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    """A git environment that reads no user or system config.

    The grading sandbox denies access to `/root/.gitconfig`, and a git that dies reading its
    config leaves the checkout exactly as it was while reporting nothing useful. Pointing
    the config at `/dev/null` makes git work the same inside and outside the sandbox.
    """
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL"] = os.devnull
    env["GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM"] = "1"
    return env


def _git(repo_root: Path, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=str(repo_root),
        env=_git_env(),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
    )


def materialize(instance: Instance, scratch: Path) -> Path:
    """Copy the pristine snapshot into the scratch directory and inject the instance bug."""
    repo = scratch / instance.repo_key
    if repo.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(repo)
    shutil.copytree(instance.repo_root, repo, symlinks=True)
    _git(repo, "reset", "--hard", "HEAD")
    _git(repo, "clean", "-qfd")
    patch_path = scratch / "bug.patch"
    patch_path.write_text(instance.bug_patch, encoding="utf-8")
    applied = _git(repo, "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(patch_path))
    if applied.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"{instance.instance_id}: bug patch did not apply: {applied.stdout[-400:]}"
        )
    return repo


def _patch_targets(patch_text: str) -> list[str]:
    """The paths a unified diff writes to (its `+++ b/...` lines)."""
    targets = []
    for line in patch_text.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            targets.append(line[len("+++ b/"):].strip())
        elif line.startswith("+++ "):
            targets.append(line[len("+++ "):].strip())
    return targets


def _escapes_checkout(target: str) -> bool:
    """True when a patch target names something outside the checkout.

    An empty path, an absolute path, or one that climbs with `..` would write outside the
    scratch tree the grader controls.
    """
    if not target or target in ("/dev/null",):
        return False
    if target.startswith("/"):
        return True
    parts = Path(target).parts
    return any(part == ".." for part in parts)


def apply_submission(repo: Path, submission: Submission, scratch: Path) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
    """Apply the rollout patch into the checkout.

    Returns (applied, notes). The run proceeds on the unpatched tree when the patch does not
    apply -- the instance's own tests still describe that tree -- but a run that passes there
    cannot be credited to the patch, so `grade_run` demotes it.
    """
    if not submission.patch.strip():
        return True, ["empty-patch: no patch in the submission; run proceeds on the unpatched tree"]
    for target in _patch_targets(submission.patch):
        if _escapes_checkout(target):
            return False, [f"patch-rejected: target leaves the checkout: {target}"]
    patch_path = scratch / "submission.patch"
    patch_path.write_text(submission.patch, encoding="utf-8")
    applied = _git(repo, "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", str(patch_path))
    if applied.returncode != 0:
        applied = subprocess.run(
            ["patch", "-p1", "--forward", "--batch", "-i", str(patch_path)],
            cwd=str(repo),
            env=_git_env(),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            text=True,
        )
    if applied.returncode == 0:
        return True, []
    tail = (applied.stdout or "").strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["no output"]
    return False, ["patch-failed: " + tail[0][:200]]


def _write_log(scratch: Path, run: RunOutput) -> None:
    """The record's artifact: the parsed transcript, plus stderr when there was any."""
    text = run.log
    if run.stderr.strip():
        text += "\n\n----- stderr -----\n" + run.stderr
    if run.timed_out:
        text += "\n\n----- timed out -----\n"
    (scratch / "pytest.log").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def _grade_record(instance: Instance, submission: Submission, scratch: Path, timeout_s: int) -> Grade:
    repo = materialize(instance, scratch)
    exam = snapshot_exam(repo, test_files(instance))
    applied, notes = apply_submission(repo, submission, scratch)
    notes = notes + restore_exam(repo, exam)

    return grade_run(

        report,
        submission.record_id,
        notes=notes,

        timed_out=run.timed_out,

            ["patch", "-p1", "--forward", "--batch", "-i", str(patch_path)],
            cwd=str(repo),
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
            text=True,
        )
    return [] if applied.returncode == 0 else ["patch-failed"]


def grade_record(instance: Instance, submission: Submission, scratch: Path, timeout_s: int = 900) -> Grade:
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    repo = materialize(instance, scratch)
    notes = apply_submission(repo, submission, scratch)
    restore_tests(repo)
    run = run_command(build_command(instance, test_files(instance)), cwd=repo, timeout_s=timeout_s)
    (scratch / "pytest.log").write_text(run.log, encoding="utf-8")
    statuses = parse_pytest_log(run.log)
    grade = grade_statuses(instance, statuses, submission.record_id, notes=notes)
    grade.notes = list(grade.notes) + [f"exit={run.exit_code}", f"seconds={run.seconds:.1f}"]
    return grade

"""Unit tests of the grading pipeline.

They run without any repository checkout: the parser, the matcher and the reward rule are fed
recorded pytest output. Run them with any interpreter that has pytest:

    python3 -m pytest tests -q
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from rlgrade.log_parse import parse_pytest_log  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.match import lookup  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.reward import grade_statuses  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.types import Instance  # noqa: E402

# Captured from a run of one of the corpus repositories.
SUMMARY_LOG = """\
============================= test session starts ==============================
collected 3 items

tests/test_core.py::test_alpha PASSED                                    [ 33%]
tests/test_core.py::test_beta FAILED                                     [ 66%]
tests/test_extra.py::test_gamma PASSED                                   [100%]

=========================== short test summary info ============================
PASSED tests/test_core.py::test_alpha
FAILED tests/test_core.py::test_beta - AssertionError: 1 != 2
PASSED tests/test_extra.py::test_gamma
========================= 2 passed, 1 failed in 0.21s ==========================
"""


def instance(tmp_path: Path, required: list[str]) -> Instance:
    return Instance(
        instance_id="demo__repo.0000.bug__x",
        repo_key="demo__repo.0000",
        repo_root=tmp_path,
        env_python=Path(sys.executable),
        bug_patch="",
        fail_to_pass=tuple(required[:1]),
        pass_to_pass=tuple(required[1:]),
    )


def test_parses_every_reported_test():
    statuses = parse_pytest_log(SUMMARY_LOG)
    assert len(statuses) == 3


def test_failed_test_is_reported_as_failed():
    statuses = parse_pytest_log(SUMMARY_LOG)
    _, status = lookup(statuses, "tests/test_core.py::test_beta")
    assert status == "FAILED"


def test_reward_is_one_when_every_required_test_passes(tmp_path):
    statuses = parse_pytest_log(SUMMARY_LOG)
    target = instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_core.py::test_alpha", "tests/test_extra.py::test_gamma"])
    grade = grade_statuses(target, statuses, record_id="r1")
    assert grade.reward == 1.0
    assert grade.label == "resolved"


def test_reward_is_zero_when_a_required_test_fails(tmp_path):
    statuses = parse_pytest_log(SUMMARY_LOG)
    target = instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_core.py::test_beta", "tests/test_core.py::test_alpha"])
    grade = grade_statuses(target, statuses, record_id="r2")
    assert grade.reward == 0.0
    assert grade.label == "unresolved"


def test_a_required_test_the_run_never_mentions_is_not_rewarded(tmp_path):
    statuses = parse_pytest_log(SUMMARY_LOG)
    target = instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_core.py::test_alpha", "tests/test_core.py::test_absent"])
    grade = grade_statuses(target, statuses, record_id="r3")
    assert grade.reward != 1.0

Now I write the full new test file. Key coverage from the plan:

1. Parser tests:
   - green log without summary section → parses → resolved 1.0 (the incident)
   - all status kinds incl. param-with-spaces, truncated XFAIL reason, teardown PASSED-then-ERROR (ERROR wins)
   - summary lines not parsed as progress (SKIPPED file:line entries)
   - phantom PASSED line → count mismatch → unscorable
   - no banner + statuses → unscorable
   - no tests ran → no statuses → unscorable
   - empty log → unscorable
   - usage error log (empty stdout) → unscorable

2. Matcher tests:
   - exact-match no-substring (required `test_email_validation` vs reported passing `..._with_none` → missing → unscorable, not resolved)

3. Reward tests:
   - missing → unscorable reward None
   - failed/skipped required → unresolved 0.0
   - XPASS counts as passed
   - timed out → unscorable
   - patch not applied + resolved run → unresolved 0.0
   - patch not applied + missing → unscorable

4. Reset tests:
   - snapshot/restore round-trip: modify/delete/add exam files incl. conftest.py, pytest.ini, helper under tests/, new test file → all undone; package source edit survives
   - root-level test file layout: root package file survives

5. Pipeline tests (end-to-end on tiny git repo built in tmp_path):
   - git init + commit pristine
   - bug patch breaks src
   - submission A fixes + adds attacking conftest → resolved
   - submission B only adds conftest → unresolved NOT resolved
   - empty patch → unresolved
   - patch traversal rejection
   - grader never raises (e.g. materialize fails → unscorable)

Let me write the end-to-end tests carefully. Building a tiny git repo in tmp_path:

```python

    _run(["git", "add", "-A"], cwd=path)
    _run(["git", "commit", "-qm", "pristine"], cwd=path)

```

Wait — with root-level `test_pkg.py` and root `pkg.py`, my exam logic: `test_pkg.py` matches `test_*.py` → exam; it's at root so `"/" in rel` is False → repo root not swept → `pkg.py` (the source) NOT in exam.

```

```

(with trailing newline). The buggy version:

That should apply with `git apply`. Good.

Submission A patch (fix + attacking conftest):
```
diff --git a/pkg.py b/pkg.py
--- a/pkg.py
+++ b/pkg.py
@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@

-    return x * 3

```

Wait — the submission patch applies on top of the bug patch. So it must reverse the bug. Good.

Attacking conftest.py addition (new file):
```
diff --git a/conftest.py b/conftest.py
new file mode 100644
--- /dev/null
+++ b/conftest.py
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+import pytest
+
+
+@pytest.hookimpl(hookwrapper=True)
+def pytest_runtest_makereport(item, call):
+    outcome = yield
+    report = outcome.get_result()
+    if report.when == "call":
+        report.outcome = "passed"
```

Hmm wait — does the makereport hookwrapper approach actually flip FAILED to PASSED in the progress output? In the corpus attacks it did (that's the documented attack). The progress line is printed from the report. Actually pytest's terminal reporter uses `pytest_runtest_logreport` with the report — hookwrapper modifying report.outcome after `makereport` returns... The corpus conftest attacks did exactly this and were reported to flip failures to passed (per my earlier investigation of the corpus tampering taxonomy). I verified this earlier: "30× untracked root `conftest.py` (hookwrapper `pytest_runtest_makereport` flipping failures to passed)". So yes.

But careful: with report.outcome = "passed", the count line will also say "N passed". So the count cross-check won't catch it — but the exam restore will (conftest.py removed before run). That's the point of the test: submission B (conftest only, no fix) → run would report test PASSED (fake) but conftest is removed → test runs honestly → FAILED → unresolved 0.0. 

For submission B the patch is only the new conftest.py (no src change). After restore removes conftest.py, the buggy pkg remains → test fails → unresolved. Good.

For submission A: fix + attacking conftest → after restore removes conftest, fixed pkg → test passes → resolved 1.0. Good.

Empty patch → (True, note) → run proceeds on buggy tree → test FAILED → unresolved 0.0. Good.

Patch traversal: a patch with `+++ b/../../outside.py` → rejected (False, note) → run proceeds on buggy tree → FAILED → unresolved 0.0, with note patch-rejected. Good.

Materialize failure → bug patch doesn't apply → RuntimeError caught → unscorable with grader-error note. Good.

Also a test for "run never reported a required node id" end-to-end? The truncated-id case is corpus data; unit level covers it.

Also test that `to_json` gives reward null for unscorable? Cheap and relevant to the contract. Let me add: `assert grade.to_json()["reward"] is None`.

Also test parse handles summary-section SKIPPED lines with file:line (not node ids) — i.e. that they're not taken as progress lines. A SKIPPED summary line `SKIPPED [1] tests/test_x.py:9: no driver` — my PROGRESS_RE requires a `[ NN%]` at the end with percent; `SKIPPED [1] tests/...` doesn't match (starts with SKIPPED, and the bracket is `[1]` not `[ 10%]`). Actually the regex anchors `^(?P<node>.*?)\s+(?P<status>...)\s*\[ NN%]`. The summary line "SKIPPED [1] tests/test_x.py:9: no driver" — node would have to be something ending before a status word... arguments.content:
"""Unit tests of the grading pipeline.

The parser, the matcher, the reward rule and the exam snapshot/restore are fed recorded
pytest output (captured verbatim from runs of the corpus repositories' own pytest) or a
tiny git repository built in a temporary directory. Run them with any interpreter that has
pytest:

    python3 -m pytest tests -q
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from rlgrade import grade_record  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.command import BASE_FLAGS, build_command  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.log_parse import parse_pytest_log  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.match import lookup  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.reset import exam_files, restore_exam, snapshot_exam  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.reward import grade_run  # noqa: E402
from rlgrade.types import Instance, Submission  # noqa: E402

# A green run under the old command flags: verbose progress lines, closing banner, and *no*
# short test summary section. The old parser read only that section, so a run like this one
# parsed as empty and was paid 0.0 -- the whole training pass zeroed on it.
GREEN_LOG_NO_SUMMARY = """\
============================= test session starts ==============================
collected 2 items

tests/test_core.py::test_alpha PASSED                                    [ 50%]
tests/test_extra.py::test_gamma PASSED                                   [100%]

============================== 2 passed in 0.05s ===============================
"""

# Every status kind pytest prints, captured verbatim: reasons in parentheses, a truncated
# reason (`(h...)`), parametrized ids containing spaces and brackets, and an `-rA` summary
# section whose SKIPPED entries are file:line, not node ids.
MIXED_LOG = """\
============================= test session starts ==============================
collected 8 items

tests/test_x.py::test_pass PASSED                                    [ 12%]
tests/test_x.py::test_fail FAILED                                    [ 25%]
tests/test_x.py::test_skip SKIPPED (no driver)                       [ 37%]
tests/test_x.py::test_xfail XFAIL (h...)                             [ 50%]
tests/test_x.py::test_xpass XPASS (still passes)                     [ 62%]
tests/test_x.py::test_param[a - b] FAILED                            [ 75%]
tests/test_x.py::test_param[x [y]] PASSED                            [ 87%]
tests/test_x.py::test_ok ERROR                                       [100%]

=========================== short test summary info ============================
PASSED tests/test_x.py::test_pass
FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_fail - assert 1 == 2
SKIPPED [1] tests/test_x.py:9: no driver
XFAIL tests/test_x.py::test_xfail - known
XPASS tests/test_x.py::test_xpass - still passes
FAILED tests/test_x.py::test_param[a - b] - assert 3 == 4
ERROR tests/test_x.py::test_ok - RuntimeError: setup died
========== 3 failed, 2 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1 xpassed, 1 error in 0.02s ==========
"""

# A teardown error reports the same node twice: PASSED, then ERROR. The later line wins.
TEARDOWN_LOG = """\
collected 1 item

test_teardown.py::test_ok PASSED                                         [100%]
test_teardown.py::test_ok ERROR                                          [100%]

=========================== short test summary info ============================
PASSED test_teardown.py::test_ok
ERROR test_teardown.py::test_ok - RuntimeError: teardown died
========================== 1 passed, 1 error in 0.01s ==========================
"""

# One more PASSED progress line than the banner accounts for -- what an injected line or a
# doctored transcript looks like to the cross-check.
PHANTOM_LOG = """\
collected 1 item

test_x.py::test_real PASSED                                              [ 50%]
test_x.py::test_phantom PASSED                                           [100%]

============================== 1 passed in 0.01s ===============================
"""

# Progress lines but no closing banner at all: output that stopped before the run finished.
NO_BANNER_LOG = """\
collected 2 items

tests/test_core.py::test_alpha PASSED                                    [ 50%]
"""

NO_TESTS_LOG = """\
============================ no tests ran in 0.00s =============================
"""


def make_instance(tmp_path: Path, required: list[str]) -> Instance:
    return Instance(
        instance_id="demo__repo.0000.bug__x",
        repo_key="demo__repo.0000",
        repo_root=tmp_path,
        env_python=Path(sys.executable),
        bug_patch="",
        fail_to_pass=tuple(required[:1]),
        pass_to_pass=tuple(required[1:]),
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parser


def test_green_log_without_summary_section_parses():
    """The incident: a passing run printed no summary section, and the old parser saw nothing."""
    report = parse_pytest_log(GREEN_LOG_NO_SUMMARY)
    assert report.statuses == {
        "tests/test_core.py::test_alpha": "PASSED",
        "tests/test_extra.py::test_gamma": "PASSED",
    }
    assert not report.inconsistent


def test_every_status_kind_parses():
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_pass"] == "PASSED"
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_fail"] == "FAILED"
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_skip"] == "SKIPPED"
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_xfail"] == "XFAIL"
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_xpass"] == "XPASS"
    # Parametrized ids with spaces and brackets must survive as whole node ids.
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_param[a - b]"] == "FAILED"
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_param[x [y]]"] == "PASSED"
    assert report.statuses["tests/test_x.py::test_ok"] == "ERROR"
    assert not report.inconsistent


def test_summary_section_is_not_parsed_as_progress():
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    # The SKIPPED summary entry is a file:line, and no summary line may become a status.
    assert "tests/test_x.py:9" not in report.statuses
    assert len(report.statuses) == 8


def test_teardown_error_later_line_wins():
    report = parse_pytest_log(TEARDOWN_LOG)
    assert report.statuses["test_teardown.py::test_ok"] == "ERROR"
    assert not report.inconsistent  # two progress lines, "1 passed, 1 error" accounts for both


def test_phantom_progress_line_is_flagged():
    report = parse_pytest_log(PHANTOM_LOG)
    assert report.statuses  # the statuses are still readable
    assert report.inconsistent  # but the banner does not account for them


def test_statuses_without_a_banner_are_flagged():
    report = parse_pytest_log(NO_BANNER_LOG)
    assert report.statuses
    assert report.inconsistent


def test_no_tests_ran_and_empty_logs_parse_empty():
    for log in (NO_TESTS_LOG, ""):
        report = parse_pytest_log(log)
        assert report.statuses == {}
        assert not report.inconsistent


def test_usage_error_stdout_is_empty():
    # pytest prints its usage errors on stderr; stdout, the parsed transcript, is empty.
    report = parse_pytest_log("")
    assert report.statuses == {}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- matcher


def test_match_is_exact_no_substring_fallback():
    """The old fallback: a required id answered by any longer id that contains it."""
    statuses = {"tests/test_x.py::test_email_validation_with_none": "PASSED"}
    key, status = lookup(statuses, "tests/test_x.py::test_email_validation")
    assert key is None
    assert status is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reward


def test_all_required_passing_is_resolved(tmp_path):
    report = parse_pytest_log(GREEN_LOG_NO_SUMMARY)
    target = make_instance(
        tmp_path, ["tests/test_core.py::test_alpha", "tests/test_extra.py::test_gamma"]
    )
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r1")
    assert grade.label == "resolved"
    assert grade.reward == 1.0


def test_a_failing_required_test_is_unresolved_zero(tmp_path):
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    target = make_instance(
        tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_pass", "tests/test_x.py::test_fail"]
    )
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r2")
    assert grade.label == "unresolved"
    assert grade.reward == 0.0


def test_skipped_and_xfail_required_tests_are_unresolved(tmp_path):
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_skip", "tests/test_x.py::test_xfail"])
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r3")
    assert grade.label == "unresolved"
    assert grade.reward == 0.0


def test_xpass_counts_as_passed(tmp_path):
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_xpass"])
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r4")
    assert grade.label == "resolved"
    assert grade.reward == 1.0


def test_a_required_id_the_run_never_reported_is_unscorable(tmp_path):
    """No neighbour's status may stand in for a required id the suite never reported."""
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_absent"])
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r5")
    assert grade.label == "unscorable"
    assert grade.reward is None
    assert grade.to_json()["reward"] is None
    assert grade.missing == ["tests/test_x.py::test_absent"]


def test_an_empty_parse_is_unscorable_not_zero(tmp_path):
    """The incident's other half: an empty parse was paid out like a genuine failure."""
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_pass"])
    grade = grade_run(target, parse_pytest_log(""), record_id="r6")
    assert grade.label == "unscorable"
    assert grade.reward is None


def test_an_inconsistent_log_is_unscorable(tmp_path):
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_real"])
    grade = grade_run(target, parse_pytest_log(PHANTOM_LOG), record_id="r7")
    assert grade.label == "unscorable"
    assert grade.reward is None


def test_a_timed_out_run_is_unscorable(tmp_path):
    report = parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG)
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_pass"])
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r8", timed_out=True)
    assert grade.label == "unscorable"
    assert grade.reward is None


def test_a_run_that_cannot_credit_the_patch_is_unresolved(tmp_path):
    report = parse_pytest_log(GREEN_LOG_NO_SUMMARY)
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_core.py::test_alpha"])
    grade = grade_run(target, report, record_id="r9", patch_applied=False)
    assert grade.label == "unresolved"
    assert grade.reward == 0.0
    assert any("did not apply" in note for note in grade.notes)


def test_missing_still_dominates_a_patch_that_did_not_apply(tmp_path):
    target = make_instance(tmp_path, ["tests/test_x.py::test_absent"])
    grade = grade_run(
        target, parse_pytest_log(MIXED_LOG), record_id="r10", patch_applied=False
    )
    assert grade.label == "unscorable"
    assert grade.reward is None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- command


def test_base_flags_keep_the_log_readable_and_complete():
    assert "--verbose" in BASE_FLAGS  # the progress lines the parser reads
    assert "-rA" in BASE_FLAGS  # the summary the count cross-check reads


def test_command_runs_only_the_required_files(tmp_path):
    target = make_instance(
        tmp_path, ["a/test_one.py::t1", "b/test_two.py::t2", "a/test_one.py::t3"]
    )
    argv = build_command(target)
    assert argv[argv.index("-m") + 1] == "pytest"
    # Manifest order, no duplicates.
    assert argv[-2:] == ["a/test_one.py", "b/test_two.py"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- exam snapshot/restore


def build_exam_repo(root: Path) -> None:
    (root / "pkg").mkdir()
    (root / "pkg" / "__init__.py").write_text("def double(x):\n    return x * 2\n")
    (root / "tests").mkdir()
    (root / "tests" / "base.py").write_text("HELPER = 1\n")
    (root / "tests" / "test_core.py").write_text("def test_core():\n    assert True\n")
    (root / "tests" / "tests.py").write_text("def test_named_tests_dot_py():\n    assert True\n")
    (root / "conftest.py").write_text("# hooks\n")


def test_restore_undoes_every_exam_change(tmp_path):
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    build_exam_repo(repo)
    snapshot = snapshot_exam(repo, ["tests/test_core.py"])

    # A rollout that stubs the required test, rewrites the conftest, deletes a helper,
    # grows a new test file, and adds a pytest.ini that would autoload a plugin.
    (repo / "tests" / "test_core.py").write_text("def test_core(*args, **kwargs):\n    pass\n")
    (repo / "conftest.py").write_text("import evil\n")  # noqa: S104 - test fixture
    (repo / "tests" / "base.py").unlink()
    (repo / "tests" / "test_evil.py").write_text("def test_evil():\n    assert True\n")
    (repo / "pytest.ini").write_text("[pytest]\naddopts = -p rollout_report_plugin\n")

    notes = restore_exam(repo, snapshot)
    assert (repo / "tests" / "test_core.py").read_text() == "def test_core():\n    assert True\n"
    assert (repo / "conftest.py").read_text() == "# hooks\n"
